# URGENT — stimulus schedule for live systems (target: before 2026-09-15)
<!-- Generated by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic); decided with Fatih on 2026-09-07 -->

## Why
Reproducibility today rests on the rosbag replay (`[replay] replay_rosbag = true`, daemon starts
`ros2 bag play` after system-stable and auto-stops at replay end). Live systems (AAS drones, TIRIS
robot) have no replay: runs are only comparable if the same commands reach the system at the same
offsets. The paper's acquisition paragraph will claim this mechanism, so it must exist and have run once.

## Design
- Settings: `[replay]` generalises to `[stimulus]`: `mode = rosbag | schedule | none`.
  `schedule_file = <path>`; each line `t_offset_s  <shell command>` (t = 0 is the system-stable instant).
  Commands are arbitrary: `ros2 topic pub --once ...`, `ros2 service call ...`, `ros2 action send_goal ...`,
  a script. `settle_s` after the last command, then auto-stop (same path as replay end).
- Daemon (python/fish/gpu.py, the replay thread): sleep to each offset, issue the command (subprocess,
  app CPU set, env of the app), log `t_sent, rc, command` to `fishlog/stimulus.log`, and emit an LTTng
  event `fish:stimulus(seq, command)` through the existing ctypes bridge (rclpy.fish_rclpy_trace uses the
  same path) so the stimuli are part of the trace on the same clock.
- Tracepoint: add `fish_stimulus` to the provider + whitelist (config/fish_events.txt), one event per
  command; the model marks it as an external stimulus (ext boundary source) — no edge inference needed
  for the WiP, just the timeline.
- Phase boundaries stay trace-derived (timers fired once / recurring callbacks' first execution); the
  schedule makes the steady-state window comparable across runs.

## Steps
1. Settings + schedule parser + daemon mode (~80 lines) — host repo.
2. `fish_stimulus` tracepoint in the overlay + whitelist entry.
3. Bring the AAS images back up (they are the live-command target): check `docker images | grep aas`,
   the AAS launch/wrapper notes (notes/*aas*), rebuild only if the overlay is older than the whitelist.
   Rule reminder: never overwrite a working image under its own name; new tag.
4. Test on TIRIS first (cheap: `ros2 topic pub` cmd_vel schedule, 60 s), then one AAS scenario.
5. Paper sentence (acquisition): "For live systems, the replay is replaced by a stimulus schedule: a list of
   timed commands ... issued at fixed offsets from the system-stable instant and recorded in the trace."

## Not in scope for the WiP
Closed-loop stimuli (react to system state), sub-ms timing claims, stimulus→response edge inference.
